title: A More Sustainable Way Forward What Teaching Could Feel Like Next
author: Findlater, Sarah
summary: Final post in the 16-part teaching wellbeing series. Teacher burnout is not about lacking resilience but about structurally unsustainable work. Sustainability means designing work humans can do well over time: bounded expectations, systems that reduce friction, protected recovery time. AI can help if used to reduce repetition and offload low-value tasks, not to accelerate pace. Real change requires system design and leadership modeling, not individual mindset shifts.
points: Teacher burnout is structural, not individual; it comes from accumulation of endless workload and unrecovered emotional labor.
Sustainability means designing work that ordinary people can do well under ordinary conditions, not heroic effort.
AI helps only when it reduces unnecessary tasks and protects recovery time, not when it increases pace or expectations.
Real change requires system design and leader modeling, not more individual resilience workshops.
Most teachers don't want an easier job; they want a possible one that doesn't require self-sacrifice.
quotes: The Teacher Wellbeing Index 2025 points to accumulation, not a single breaking point.
Most teachers are not struggling because they lack resilience or commitment.
Schools that depend on brilliance or burnout eventually run out of both.
Used well, AI does not make teachers do more. It helps them carry less.
Teaching is ridiculous and wonderful work. It deserves systems that allow people to keep doing it well.” Archived from Leading and Learning Conversations on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
